To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nutrient content of mucilage from cactus pear (Opuntia spp.) cladodes is influenced by both the cultivar and the harvest month.
Opuntia mucilage powders are highly soluble, low kilojoule, mineral-rich, and are produced from an easily cultivable plant.
the Opuntia robust cultivar has a higher nutrient content than Opuntia ficuss-indica and that Opuntia robust harvested in February is the most optimal time for harvesting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel functional food ingredient, which is a natural, low-kilocalorie, low-fat, high-mineral ingredient that is produced in an environmentally sustainable way.
the production of a low-kilojole, functional, mineral-rich, natural ingredient that could be added to functional foods to enhance the nutritional value of these products.

the production of functional food products from a crop that is grown in marginal environments, and the use of a natural, low-kJ, low-cost ingredient that can be used to replace high-energy ingredients in food products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mucilage from Opuntia spp., particularly Opuntia ficuss-indica and Opuntia robust, are low-kilojoul and mineral-rich ingredients with potential health benefits.

Opuntia robust Robusta mucilage harvested in February has the lowest energy content, highest protein, extractable and total fat content, highest mineral and potassium content, and is a highly soluble functional ingredient.
Opuntia mucilage powder from O. robusta harvested in February is the preferred cultivar and harvest time for a high-quality, low-kilo joul, mineral-rich functional food ingredient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Opuntia mucilage is a novel functional ingredient with a high nutritional profile.
Opuntia robusto Robusta cactus pear mucilage is the most suitable mucilage for use in food products.
mucilage extracted from cacti cladodes is a novel, low-kilo-joule, cost effective texture-modifying functional ingredient in functional food.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Opuntia robustas mucilage is the preferred source of cactus pear mucilage, as the harvest month and cultivar influence its nutritional value.
mucilage from O. ficus-indica cultivars is a good source of soluble fibre, while O. robusta mucilage is a good source for energy-restricted, mineral-rich diets.
the nutrient composition of Opuntia mucilage is cultivar- and harvest time-dependent.
